# Bounded Mahler measure in the divisible group generated by conjugate units

<a id="statement"></a>
## Products with arbitrary rational exponents

Fix \(M,N>0\).
Let \(x\) be a reciprocal unit of positive logarithmic Mahler measure at most \(M\), of degree \(d\), with no torsion quotient between distinct conjugates.
Choose representatives \(x_i\) from the \(v=d/2\) inverse pairs.
Suppose \(y\) is nontorsion, \(m(y)\le N\), and for some \(n\ge1\),
\[
                          y^n=\zeta\prod_i x_i^{a_i},\qquad
                    a_i\in\mathbb Z,\quad \zeta\text{ a root of unity}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(d\) in terms of \(M,N\), the following necessary conditions hold, uniformly in the root of unity and in all exponents, including \(n\).

* If the Galois group contains all even inversions on each [canonical block](Yin_C_G0345_v270.md#statement), at most one \(a_i\) is nonzero.
  For ordinary powers (\(n=1\)) with at least two occupied labels one has the direct estimate \(m(y)\ge (b-1)\max_i|a_i|\,m(x)\), independently of \(N\), where \(b\) is the common block size.
* In the other [sign alternative](Yin_C_G0345_v274.md#statement), choose the representatives according to one of the two canonical orientations on each block.
  Then \(a_i\) is constant within each block with at most one exceptional coordinate across **all** blocks.
  Thus \(y^n\) is a product of powers of oriented block products and at most one power of a single conjugate, up to torsion.
  In particular if all the block products are torsion, only a rational power of a single conjugate modulo torsion can remain.

In either sign alternative, if any relation as displayed has at least two nonzero coordinates in the first case or fails the stated constant-coordinate condition in the second, then \(m(y)\to\infty\) uniformly as \(d\to\infty\) with \(m(x)\le M\).
These restrictions include roots of mixed monomials of arbitrarily high order.
Earlier [sharp monomial estimates](Yin_C_G0345_v74.md#statement) for two exterior roots in one block concern integer powers and use that prescribed signature.

<a id="closure"></a>
## How a solvable extension bounds the degree after compression

The following comparison also applies to elements outside the divisible group.
Write \(b\) for the block size and \(u=v/b\) for the block count of \(x\), taking \(d\) sufficiently large that \(b>u+2\).
For any \(y\) of positive measure at most \(N\) whose rational splitting field is contained in a finite Galois extension solvable over the splitting field of \(x\) (in a common normal extension over \(\mathbb Q\)), let \(D\) be the degree of its torsion-class product.
Then
\[
                                 D\ll_N b(\log(3b))^{212}.                  \tag{1}
\]
Here the ambient extension is assumed Galois over \(\mathbb Q\), containing both splitting fields, and solvable over that of \(x\).
For the displayed radical relation, take \(n\) times the order of \(\zeta\), adjoin roots of unity of that order and the corresponding radicals of all conjugate products.
The normal extension so obtained is solvable over the splitting field of \(x\) by its cyclotomic and abelian radical layers.

A nonabelian simple section (a quotient of a subgroup) of a group extension is a section of its kernel or quotient.
Indeed the image of the subgroup's intersection with the kernel in the simple quotient is trivial or surjective.
This applies also to direct products by induction.
The splitting group of \(x\) has an elementary abelian sign kernel and a label quotient contained in \(S_b\wr S_u\).
No alternating group \(A_j\) with \(j>b\) can be a section, by the extension observation and the orders of the symmetric groups of degrees \(b,u\).
The same exclusion holds for the ambient group and its quotient acting on the conjugates of \(y\).
If \(D\) is large depending on \(N\), the [independent alternating factors](Yin_C_G0345_v270.md#partition) of the compressed number include \(A_{b_y}\), where the [two-coordinate height bound](Yin_C_G0345_v264.md#block) gives \(b_y\gg_N D/(\log(3D))^{212}\).
Thus \(b_y\le b\).
For large \(D\) this first gives \(b\gg_N\sqrt D\), and then substitution in the logarithm gives (1).
Bounded \(D\) also satisfies (1).

<a id="inversions"></a>
## Orbit size and height with independent sign changes

Work in the rational multiplicative vector space modulo torsion.
The number of distinct conjugate images of \(y\) there is precisely \(D\), by the [class-product argument](Yin_C_G0345_v264.md#labels).
Multiplication of a vector by \(n\ne0\) preserves its orbit cardinality.
Thus \(D\) is the orbit size of the vector represented by \(\prod x_i^{a_i}\), regardless of \(n\).
With all blockwise even sign changes, the representatives are [multiplicatively independent](Yin_C_G0345_v274.md#statement), so this is the orbit size of the exponent vector itself under signed permutations.

Inside an occupied block with \(k\) nonzero entries there are at least \(\binom bk2^k\) images for \(1\le k<b\) and at least \(2^{b-1}\) for \(k=b\).
Indeed the alternating group is transitive on supports of a given size, and an unused coordinate absorbs the required parity of sign changes.
These possibilities multiply over blocks because the label image contains the direct product of alternating groups and the sign kernel contains each even sign subgroup independently.
Each occupied block contributes at least \(2b\), and each with \(k\ge2\) contributes at least \(2b(b-1)\) for sufficiently large \(b\).
For \(2\le k\le b-2\) use \(\binom bk\ge\binom b2\), and for the last two sizes use their exponential sign counts.
With \(t\) occupied blocks there are at least \(u/t\) images of their set by transitivity on blocks.
If just one block is occupied with \(k\ge2\), this proves \(D\ge2v(b-1)\).
If \(t\ge2\), then \(D\ge(u/t)(2b)^t\ge2ub^2\).
Both contradict (1) as \(b\to\infty\), since \(v\ge b\).

For the direct height estimate put \(s_i=\log|x_i|\).
Under a uniform random even sign vector on each block the signs \(\epsilon_i\) have pairwise zero correlation for \(b\ge3\).
For any fixed permutation and inversion of the representatives, write \(s'_i\) for the transported signed logarithms.
Then
\[
     \mathbb E_\epsilon\left|\sum_i a_i\epsilon_i s'_i\right|
          \ \ge\ \left|\mathbb E_\epsilon\,\epsilon_j\sum_i a_i\epsilon_i s'_i\right|
          = |a_j s'_j|.
\]
Averaging over all Galois images, the mean of \(|s'_j|\) equals \(2h(x)\), since \(x\) is a unit.
The left side averages to twice the height of the monomial, again a unit.
A torsion twist preserves that height and has degree at least \(D\).
The bound follows from \(D\ge2v(b-1)\) and \(d=2v\).

<a id="orientations"></a>
## Coefficients modulo the constant vector of each oriented block

In the orientation alternative, pass from formal exponent vectors to the quotient by the constant vectors on the individual blocks.
The resulting vector is determined by the multiplicative element modulo torsion, since [all relations restrict to one sign line per block](Yin_C_G0345_v270.md#rank).
In the chosen canonical orientations any nonzero projected relation is constant: its line is equivariant, and the localized alternating group permutes the oriented labels naturally and transitively.
Indeed a perfect transitive alternating group fixes each vector on an invariant rational line.
Its fixed vectors in the natural permutation representation are constant.
Equivalently one may lift the product of the independent alternating factors to the signed group stabilizing each block and take the eventual derived subgroup of this preimage.
It still surjects onto the product and fixes the two orientations of every block, since their permutations form an abelian quotient.
Thus one gets pure alternating permutations in all blocks independently on the quotient of formal exponent vectors.
Its orbit size bounds \(D\) from below.

For each nonconstant block vector, sorting its multiset of coefficients gives at least \(b\) images under \(A_b\).
Equality of permuted vectors modulo constants entails actual equality, because the sum of entries is invariant.
If there is more than one outlier from a common value (meaning the pattern is neither constant nor one exception), there are at least \(\binom b2\) images for large \(b\).
If some value occurs between two and \(b-2\) times, move its positions by \(A_b\).
If all values are distinct, the orbit has size \(b!/2\).
With \(t\ge2\) nonconstant blocks this gives \(D\ge (u/t)b^t\ge ub^2/2\).
With just one nonconstant block having no value of multiplicity \(b-1\), it gives \(D\ge u\binom b2\).
Either violates (1) for large \(d\), since the uniform block-size bound forces \(b\to\infty\).
This leaves the asserted single exceptional coordinate and proves the conclusion.
